stories.headline: OpenAI amends Pentagon deal with Fourth Amendment surveillance ban after backlash
key_facts: OpenAI and Pentagon added explicit Fourth Amendment language banning 'deliberate tracking, surveillance, or monitoring of U.S. persons or nationals'
Amendment extends ban to commercially acquired personal data (geolocation, browsing, financial) previously not covered
Pentagon affirmed OpenAI services will not be used by NSA; intelligence agency use requires separate contract modification
Altman admitted deal 'looked opportunistic and sloppy' and shouldn't have been rushed out on Friday
Original deal signed hours after Trump ordered federal agencies to stop using Anthropic and Pentagon designated Anthropic a 'Supply-Chain Risk to National Security'
573 Google employees and 93 OpenAI employees signed open letter titled 'We Will Not Be Divided' backing Anthropic's red lines

stories.headline: DeepSeek V4 multimodal model expected this week, optimized for Huawei chips
key_facts: DeepSeek plans to release V4 this week, its first major model launch since January 2025
V4 is multimodal with text, image, and video generation capabilities
Rumored specs include ~1 trillion parameters with ~32B active (MoE), 1M token context window
Optimized for Huawei and Cambricon chips rather than Nvidia; DeepSeek has not shown V4 to US chipmakers
Leaked API pricing suggests $0.27 per million input tokens — roughly 50x cheaper than frontier US models
Launch timed ahead of China's annual 'Two Sessions' parliamentary meetings starting March 4

stories.headline: Cognition previews SWE-1.6 coding model: 11% better on SWE-Bench Pro at 950 tok/s
key_facts: SWE-1.6 scores 11% higher than SWE-1.5 on SWE-Bench Pro while maintaining 950 tokens/second speed
Built on same pre-trained model as SWE-1.5 but trained with two orders of magnitude more compute
Served via Cerebras at 950 tok/s — 6x faster than Haiku 4.5 and 13x faster than Sonnet 4.5
Training runs 6x faster than SWE-1.5 using NVFP4 precision for 2-3x throughput gains over BF16/FP8
New behaviors emerged from RL: improved codebase exploration and task tracking, but also 'overthinking and excessive self-verification'
Currently in early preview with limited access; Devin 2.2 released Feb 24 with desktop support and 3x faster startup

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Import Memory to transfer context from ChatGPT and Gemini
key_facts: New feature at claude.com/import-memory lets users export stored memories from ChatGPT, Gemini, or Copilot and import into Claude
Works by pasting an Anthropic-provided prompt into rival chatbot, which dumps all stored memories into transferable text
Memory feature expanded to free Claude users, previously limited to paid subscribers
Claude memories are encrypted and not used for model training; users can export their full memory at any time
Strategic timing amid Anthropic's federal government ban — aims to attract individual and enterprise users from rivals

stories.headline: ARC-AGI-3 interactive reasoning benchmark launches March 25; frontier AI scored 0% in preview
key_facts: ARC-AGI-3 launches March 25, 2026, as the first interactive reasoning benchmark — agents must explore, learn, plan, and adapt in novel game environments
In preview period, leading AI systems scored 0% while human participants achieved 100% across released levels
Over 1,200 human participants completed 3,900+ games; top AI submission (StochasticGoose from Tufa Labs) scored 12.58%
Measures action efficiency: how many actions it takes to reach a goal, enabling formal human vs AI comparison for first time
Major format change from ARC-AGI-1/2 static puzzles; tests exploration, goal directedness, memory, and alignment
Will include 1,000+ levels across 150+ environments

stories.headline: Sakana AI's Doc-to-LoRA internalizes documents into model weights in under 1 second
key_facts: Doc-to-LoRA generates LoRA adapters in a single forward pass, reducing update latency from minutes to under 1 second
Internalizes context at 4x the base model's native context window with near-perfect accuracy
Cuts KV-cache memory from 12+ GB to under 50 MB for long documents
Companion Text-to-LoRA generates task-specific adapters from natural language description alone, matching oracle fine-tuned adapters
Both methods use trained hypernetworks to meta-learn LoRA matrix generation — no retraining needed
Code and paper released open-source (arXiv: 2602.15902)

stories.headline: Inception's Mercury 2 diffusion LLM generates 1,000+ tokens/sec via parallel token refinement
key_facts: Mercury 2 generates all tokens simultaneously via iterative denoising passes, achieving 1,000+ tokens/second
5x faster than leading speed-optimized autoregressive LLMs; quality trails frontier models by 5-15% on complex reasoning but matches on structured output
Uses masking-based corruption process for discrete tokens instead of Gaussian noise on embeddings
Denoising steps adjust dynamically: 8 for simple outputs, 16-20 for complex reasoning
GPQA score of 0.7; production-ready with dramatically lower inference cost due to parallel generation
Released February 24, 2026 by Inception Labs

stories.headline: ICLR 2026 hosts first-ever workshop on recursive AI self-improvement as field goes from theory to production
key_facts: World's first workshop dedicated exclusively to recursive self-improvement (RSI), held at ICLR 2026 in Rio de Janeiro April 26-27
LLM agents now rewrite their own codebases, scientific discovery pipelines run continual fine-tuning, and robotics stacks patch controllers from telemetry
Workshop covers experience learning, synthetic data pipelines, multimodal agentic systems, weak-to-strong generalization, and inference-time scaling
Unifies STaR, SPIN, Reflexion, GANs and AlphaZero as specific realizations of self-play operators that satisfy stability conditions
Paper tracks accept production loop documentation and data engine architectures integrating synthetic data, retrieval/memory, and continual updates
Organizers note RSI is 'no longer speculative — it is becoming a concrete systems problem'
